question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{49-5x}$ at the point where $x=0.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=49-5x.$ Then $y=\sqrt{u}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-5.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (-5) \\  & =-\frac{5}{2\sqrt{49-5x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=0} & ={(-\frac{5}{2\sqrt{49-5x}})|}_{x=0} \\  & =\frac{-5}{2\sqrt{49-5(0)}} \\  & =\frac{-5}{2\sqrt{49}} \\  & =-\frac{5}{14}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{91+5x}$ at the point where $x=-2.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=91+5x.$ Then $y=\sqrt{u}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=5.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (5) \\  & =\frac{5}{2\sqrt{91+5x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=-2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=-2} & ={(\frac{5}{2\sqrt{91+5x}})|}_{x=-2} \\  & =\frac{5}{2\sqrt{91+5(-2)}} \\  & =\frac{5}{2\sqrt{81}} \\  & =\frac{5}{18}.\end{aligned}
$$
